_meta.companion: data/telescopes/yerkes.md (same content as Markdown). Structure: sources{key: cite, file, url}; yerkes{title, telescope{objective, pupil, foci[1]}, params, color_curve (machine-readable secondary spectrum), not_found, conflicts, notes}.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src, loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/yerkes/ (ADS article scans). Quotes reproduce the ADS OCR text layer verbatim, artefacts included (e.g. "io''6" for 10".6, "d=" for plus-minus); check "ocr" = matched against tesseract OCR of the rendered page (recipes in ocr_recipes); figure_readoff = read from the page image by eye. derived = arithmetic done here. INFERRED = reasoned, not stated. Nothing is filled from memory.

color_curve.source: FOX Table IV ("Color-Curve of Forty-Inch Objective", objective alone), mean of three zones (r = 450, 310, 170 mm); focal readings in mm on an arbitrary scale (Fox: "Small values of the focal setting indicate short focal length")
color_curve.derived_note: DERIVED: defocus = reading - minimum reading of the same plate (Arcturus 445.28 mm at 5732 A; Vega 445.18 mm at 5760 A); geometric blur-circle diameter = defocus x D/f = defocus / 19.05; in arcsec = blur x 10.657 "/mm. Values were read from the page image and cross-checked with the OCR (OCR-mangled cells such as 4383 "4QOT.92" and 4308 "SoT.45" were read visually).

not_found: Glass types of the crown and flint (catalogue names, refractive indices, dispersions): only "disks furnished by Mantois of Paris" (H97). The Brashear account of the discs (Popular Astronomy 1, 1893-94, cited by H97) was not obtained (ADS returned HTTP 504).
An unvignetted or corrected field of view of the objective, and the focal-surface curvature.
A published secondary-spectrum coefficient in modern form (the colour curves of FOX and HE99 are the measurements; the defocus/blur values here are DERIVED).
Barnard's temperature results (B17: "an investigation, which is not yet printed").
conflicts: Focal length: 19354 mm at 50 F (B17, micrometer; used by FOX) vs 1936 cm (HE99, star trails) vs 19.36 m (S10) vs "very nearly 62 feet" = 18.90 m (H97). Lens-to-focus distances 18966 mm (crown surface) and 18793 mm (lens-space centre) are not focal lengths (B17).
Lens separation: 8 3/8 in (H97, page image) vs 8.6 in = 218 mm (B17) vs "about seven inches" (K96, 1895 test, before the lenses were re-positioned).
Plate scale: 1" = 0.0937 mm -> 10.67"/mm (B17) vs 10.6"/mm (S10) vs 10.657"/mm DERIVED from 19354 mm.
Clear aperture: 40 in = 1016 mm (DERIVED) vs "102 cm" (HE99, rounded).
notes: Pupil for the explorer: a filled circle of D = 1.016 m (eps = 0, no vanes): the diffraction pattern is the pure Airy pattern. Pedagogically the dominant aberration is chromatic: the colour curve (yerkes.color_curve) moves the focus by ~13 mm at H-beta and ~89 mm at H-delta relative to the best (5700 A) focus, i.e. geometric blur circles of ~7" and ~50" -- far larger than the 0.14" Airy radius at 5500 A (DERIVED 1.22 x 550e-9 / 1.016 rad).
Reflections: none (refractor); 4 glass-air surfaces. F = 19.354/1.016 = f/19.05 (DERIVED).
The objective was accepted in October 1895 after Keeler's test (K96), shipped to Williams Bay and first used on 1897 May 21 (HC97); Fox (1908) used the Hartmann test (T < 0.5).
